# One-cap base-moment correction of a compatible enlargement

This note gives an exact finite linear program, its local gauge, and an
actual convex-cut realization for correcting the base centroid after
fiberwise Minkowski enlargement. It then bounds the resulting continuous
centroid motion and cap losses. The depth conclusion requires explicit
slack; it does not establish feasibility at an active zero-slack depth
constraint or a general retained fraction.

Throughout this note the mixed measure is full fiber volume, so q=d>=1.
Let D subset C be ambient convex bodies, let P be the finite set of
positive d-volume integer fibers of D, and suppose the TRUE mixed
centroid of D is g=(j,c), with integer j. Write

    m=mu_D(S)>0, d_z=|D_z|>0, v_z=z-j,
    U=span{v_z:z in P}, Q=conv{v_z:z in P}.

Because sum d_z v_z=0 with all d_z positive, zero belongs to relint Q.
Also j belongs to P, by convexity and the positive-volume Minkowski
average of the fibers. All relative statements below are taken in U.

## 1. The actual compatible enlargement

For one common parameter 0<=t<=1 set

    E_z(t)=(1-t)D_z+t C_z, z in P.                    (1)

The argument in Section 5 of
`candidate 149b5f35c717786d`
shows that these are exactly the positive integer traces of a convex
subbody E(t) subset C. Briefly, P is lattice-convex, and every integer
convex combination w=sum lambda_z z satisfies

    sum lambda_z E_z(t) subset (1-t)D_w+t C_w.

Their lifted convex hull therefore has precisely the prescribed traces
and no further integer bases. If its base affine span is deficient,
the exact one-sided ambient thickening from the cited note preserves
all integer traces. In particular mu_E>=mu_D, even if the chosen
ambient realizations are not nested away from integer bases.

More generally, the results below apply to ANY actually realized E
whose mixed measure enlarges mu_D and whose positive bases are P. Put

    w_z=|E_z|, delta=sum_z(w_z-d_z),
    m_E=m+delta, b=sum_z w_z v_z.                    (2)

Thus b is the unnormalized base-moment error. It is a vector in U.

## 2. The minimum correction mass and its exact dual

Define

    r_*(b;w)=min {sum_z s_z:
                  0<=s_z<=w_z, sum_z s_z v_z=b}.   (3)

The feasible set is nonempty: the added masses s_z=w_z-d_z are feasible.
Compactness gives a minimum and

    0<=r_*<=delta.                                  (4)

Writing retained masses as w_z-s_z gives the equivalent formula

    r_*=m_E-T_j(E),
    T_j(E)=max {sum_z t_z:0<=t_z<=w_z,
                            sum_z t_z v_z=0}.       (5)

Finite linear-programming duality also gives the attained dual

    r_*=max_(a in U)
          [a.b-sum_z w_z(a.v_z-1)_+].               (6)

Indeed use the Lagrangian sum s_z+a.(b-sum s_z v_z). Its minimum
over each interval [0,w_z] is -w_z(a.v_z-1)_+. Standard finite LP
duality applies because (3) is feasible and bounded; no smoothness,
strict feasibility, or full base rank is required. Equivalently (6)
is a finite piecewise-linear concave dual with a maximizer. A dual
maximizer need not be unique or uniformly bounded along a family.

## 3. Every correction is realized by one actual convex cut

Fix any nonzero continuous normal u. A feasible vector in (3), of
total mass r, has ordinary base first moment

    sum_z z s_z=r j+b.                              (7)

Apply `candidate 46f947c28385c3ea` to E,
the prescribed normal u, and the target moments (r,rj+b). It gives
one finite ambient closed halfspace H, with continuous normal u, such
that the actual removed measure nu=mu_E restricted to H has precisely
these moments. The theorem realizes the moments; it does not in general
realize the individual selected masses s_z.

Let H^- be its complementary CLOSED halfspace and put D'=E intersect H^-.
The shared hyperplane has zero d-volume on every integer fiber, because
u is nonzero. Hence D' has exactly

    m'=m_E-r,    integral z dmu_(D')=m' j.           (8)

In particular, choose r=r_*. Then m'>=m>0. Positive retained fiber
volume cannot lie entirely on the cut hyperplane, so D' contains a
point strictly in H^-. Interior points of the ambient body E approach
that point and eventually stay in H^-; thus D' is an actual ambient
convex body. Its true centroid is (j,c') in D' intersect Lambda.

This is an exact convex realization at finite cap parameters, including
boundary targets of the moment polytope. There is no limit of caps or
independently trimmed fiber family. In general D' need NOT contain the
old mixed source D: the same corrective cap may delete old mass while
retaining added mass elsewhere.

## 4. The local correction gauge and the exact first-order criterion

Define the nonnegative cone program

    rho_Q(b)=min {sum_z s_z:s_z>=0,
                            sum_z s_z v_z=b}.       (9)

It is precisely the Minkowski gauge of Q:

    rho_Q(b)=inf{r>=0:b in rQ}
            =max {a.b:a in U, a.v_z<=1 for all z}.  (10)

For U={0}, set rho_Q(0)=0. Otherwise 0 in relint Q makes this a
finite continuous, positively homogeneous, possibly asymmetric gauge
on U. To see (10) directly, any nonzero feasible mass r in (9)
represents b/r as a convex combination of the v_z; conversely any such
convex combination gives coefficients in (9). The polar support formula
is finite-dimensional separation of the compact convex body Q.

Always rho_Q(b)<=r_*(b;w). Moreover,

    rho_Q(b)<=min_z w_z  ==>  r_*(b;w)=rho_Q(b).     (11)

Choose an optimal representation in (9). Each coefficient is bounded
by their nonnegative total rho_Q(b), so all capacities are respected
under the displayed hypothesis. This proves (11), including equality
at the capacity threshold. It is a sufficient exact local regime,
not a necessary characterization of all inactive capacities.

For a differentiable enlargement at t=0 write

    w_z(t)=d_z+t a_z+o(t),  a_z>=0,
    A=sum_z a_z, b_1=sum_z a_z v_z.                 (12)

All original d_z are positive, so (11) applies for all sufficiently
small t>=0. Continuity and homogeneity of the gauge yield

    r_*(t)=t rho_Q(b_1)+o(t),
    m'(t)=m+t[A-rho_Q(b_1)]+o(t).                   (13)

For the Minkowski path (1), the coefficients are exact mixed-volume
derivatives

    a_z=d[V(D_z[d-1],C_z)-|D_z|]>=0.

If A>0, its added-base mean b_1/A lies in Q. There is strict first-order
retained gain precisely when rho_Q(b_1)<A. In positive base rank this
is equivalent to b_1/A belonging to relint Q; equality corresponds to
the relative boundary. In rank zero every A>0 gives strict gain.
For example a_j>0 gives strict gain: the added-base mean has positive
weight at v_j=0, an interior point of Q. No existence of such a growth
direction is asserted.

More explicitly, in positive rank the dual (10) says that equality
rho_Q(b_1)=A occurs exactly when some a obeying a.v_z<=1 has
a.v_z=1 at EVERY index with a_z>0. Thus first-order correction loses
all added mass only when the first-order additions are supported on
one proper exposed face of Q. This is an exact finite base obstruction,
not a claim about preservation of the depth constraint.

## 5. True centroid displacement and uniform cap-loss control

Let alpha=mu_E-mu_D, of mass delta, and let nu be the actual corrective
cap measure of mass r. Then, as measures,

    mu_(D')=mu_D+alpha-nu.

By (8) its base centroid is j, and its continuous centroid satisfies

    c'-c=[integral (x-c)dalpha-integral (x-c)dnu]/m'. (14)

If R_0 bounds |x-c| on both changed sources, then

    |c'-c|<=R_0(delta+r)/m'.                        (15)

Let L_0 be a uniform upper bound on the sum of all (d-1)-section
volumes of the original fibers D_z. This is finite by enclosing each
fiber in a fixed Euclidean ball; for d=1 one can take |P|. Normalize
any nonvertical cap to unit continuous normal. Moving its through-point
threshold from (j,c) to (j,c') changes the threshold in every fiber by
at most |c'-c|. Coarea therefore bounds lost ORIGINAL mass by
L_0|c'-c|, uniformly over every integer tilt. A vertical cap is unchanged
by this continuous displacement.

Write

    sigma=inf_(H contains (j,c))[mu_D(H)-beta m]>=0,
    r_D=nu(D intersect Lambda)<=r.

For every closed cap through the new centroid,

    mu_(D')(H)>=beta m+sigma-r_D-L_0|c'-c|.

Caps merely containing the centroid have no smaller mass than the
parallel through-centroid cap. Consequently the EXACT sufficient
slack condition is

    r_D+beta(delta-r)+L_0|c'-c|<=sigma.              (16)

A criterion depending only on the coarse quantities is

    beta delta+(1-beta)r
         +L_0 R_0(delta+r)/(m+delta-r)<=sigma.       (17)

The first term r_D in (16) is actual deleted old mass, not the total
added mass or an assumed zero. Both (16) and (17) follow from actual
signed source moments, not a comparison of section and volume laws.
They do not imply depth feasibility when sigma=0. If sigma>0 and the
strict gain criterion in (13) holds, every sufficiently small correction
has greater mass and still satisfies the same depth constraint. This
gives a necessary condition on such an extracted maximizer, conditional
on an available growth direction; it is not a global extraction theorem.

## 6. Exact correction of the intermediate-drifting rectangle family

Take bases -1,0,1 in n=1,d=2. The endpoint fibers of D are [0,1]^2,
its middle fiber is D_0=C_0=[0,3] times [0,3/2], and

    C_-1=[0,4] times [0,1],  C_1=[0,2]^2.

Both lifted hulls are actual convex bodies, D subset C. The midpoint
of C's endpoint fibers is exactly C_0, and D's endpoint midpoint lies
in D_0. Both endpoint bodies have base mean zero. The compatible path is

    E_-1(t)=[0,1+3t] times [0,1],
    E_0(t)=C_0, E_1(t)=[0,1+t]^2.

Its masses and base moment are

    m_E=13/2+5t+t^2, b=t^2-t, Q=[-1,1].

For 0<=t<=1, rho_Q(b)=t-t^2<=1/4 and all capacities are at least 1.
Thus r_*=t-t^2 exactly. The single removal cap

    H_t={x_1-3(z+1)>=(1+t)^2}                       (18)

removes only the rightmost strip of width t-t^2 from E_-1. Its middle
and right thresholds are strictly beyond those fibers. The retained
integer fibers are therefore exactly

    [0,(1+t)^2] times [0,1],  C_0,  [0,1+t]^2.

Their endpoint areas agree, so the retained base mean is zero, and

    m'=13/2+4t+2t^2.

Here the corrected mixed source actually contains D; the cap deletes
only added mass. Thus this example has strict retained gain throughout
0<t<=1. These uncentered rectangles are a moment-control example;
no local-depth claim about them is needed.

## 7. A centered rectangle variation with certified depth slack

Center each rectangle in Section 6 at the continuous origin instead.
Thus D_-1=D_1=[-1/2,1/2]^2 and
D_0=C_0=[-3/2,3/2] times [-3/4,3/4], while C_-1 has side lengths
4,1 and C_1 side lengths 2,2. D is centrally symmetric in the full
ambient space, with mass 13/2 and true centroid (0,0). Every containing
closed cap therefore has mass at least 13/4.

The same moment correction r=t-t^2 is realized by removing

    x_1-3(z+1)>=b_t, b_t=1/2+t/2+t^2.              (19)

Only the left fiber is trimmed, to the x_1 interval
[-(1+3t)/2,b_t]. Its length is (1+t)^2 and its center is -r/2.
The corrected mixed body contains D for every t in [0,1], has base
centroid zero, mass m'=13/2+4t+2t^2, and continuous centroid

    c'_1=-(1+t)^2 t(1-t)/(2m'), c'_2=0.             (20)

The sum of the diameters of D's three planar fibers is
2 sqrt(2)+(3/2)sqrt(5)<7, a valid total chord-length bound. At t=1/10,

    m'=173/25, c'_1=-1089/138400.

Every closed cap through this new true centroid thus has original
D-mass, and hence corrected-body mass, at least

    13/4-7(1089/138400)=442177/138400
        > (4/9)(173/25)=692/225.                    (21)

This is an explicit actual convex correction that preserves local
gamma_2 depth and gains mass. It is a strict-slack example, not an
active extremizer: the initial mass 13/2 already exceeds half of the
original C mass 25/2. The general zero-slack and retained-fraction
questions are not settled by (21).

The rational rectangle identities and the strict inequality (21) are
checked by `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_rectangle_one_cap_moment_correction.py`.

## 8. Saturation away from one base face at a strict-slack maximizer

There is a further necessary condition with no smooth-boundary
hypothesis. Suppose D is a mass-maximizing extracted body under the
integer-centroid and local beta-depth constraints, and suppose its
uniform depth slack sigma is strictly positive. Let

    G={z in P:D_z is a proper subset of C_z}.

Either G is empty, or G is contained in ONE proper exposed face of
conv(P). Consequently the centroid fiber is saturated, D_j=C_j,
and so is every fiber at a base outside that face.

Here are all needed implications. Proper inclusion of full-dimensional
compact convex fibers gives |C_z|>|D_z|. Brunn--Minkowski along (1)
gives

    w_z(t)^(1/d)>=(1-t)d_z^(1/d)+t|C_z|^(1/d),

so differentiation at zero yields

    a_z>=d d_z^((d-1)/d)(|C_z|^(1/d)-d_z^(1/d))>0.

When the two fibers are equal, a_z=0. Thus G is exactly the support
of the nonnegative first-order additions. If it is nonempty, A>0.
Strict first-order corrected gain is ruled out by maximality and
the O(t) sufficient depth cost (17). Therefore rho_Q(b_1)=A.
The last dual characterization in Section 4 puts every v_z with
z in G on one exposed face a.v_z=1 of Q. This face is proper since
0 belongs to relint Q. In rank zero all positive additions give
strict gain, so only G empty is possible.

For example, if the original C fibers restricted to P also have
base centroid j, then G must be empty. Otherwise the positive full
volume additions |C_z|-d_z are supported on that same face, giving

    a.sum_z (|C_z|-d_z)(z-j)
        =sum_z (|C_z|-d_z)>0,

contrary to the two base centroids being equal. This corollary concerns
only the positive base set of the extraction; it does not say that
all positive original C fibers have been retained. Most importantly,
it still requires sigma>0 and supplies no stationarity assertion for
the active zero-slack case.
